description: Byte budgets for the artifacts that reach a user or a peer. `npm run artifact-sizes:check` measures each one, fails above its budget, and warns when it drifts past `warnRatio` of the recorded measurement. Baselines are re-recorded with `npm run artifact-sizes:baseline`.

rationale.whyNothingCoveredThis: size-rules.json exempts `**/*.bundle`, `**/*.bundle.mjs`, and `**/*.generated.mjs` outright, and scripts/analysis/generated-paths.mjs excludes generated trees from every other analysis gate. Both exclusions are right for what they do — you cannot reduce a bundle's complexity by editing it — but together they meant the two largest files in the repository, 11.4 MB and 10.9 MB of shipped host runtime, were measured by nothing at all. `generated-freshness` proves those bundles are current. It says nothing about how big they are.
rationale.whyItMatters: TwistedPear distributes over Reticulum, including LoRa-class links, and installs onto mobile hosts. Shipped bytes are a user-visible property here in a way they are not for a server application: a bundle that quietly doubles is a install that fails on a metered connection and a mini-app that will not transfer.
rationale.whyBudgetsNotARatchet: A may-only-shrink ratchet is right for findings, which should trend to zero. A bundle legitimately grows as features land, so a monotonic floor would fail on every honest change and be routed around within a month — the failure mode this repository already documented for a benchmark floor pinned to the fastest number ever seen. A budget is a reviewed ceiling with headroom: ordinary growth passes, and crossing the ceiling is a decision someone makes on purpose by editing this file.
rationale.whyWarnBand: The ceiling alone says nothing until the day it fires, which is the other failure this repository has already recorded — a pass/fail against a distant cliff cannot tell you which of a hundred commits caused the drift. The warn band reports movement while it is still cheap to explain.
rationale.whyCommittedOnly: Only tracked files are budgeted. `apps/harness-mobile/worklet/*-wasm.generated.mjs` are build output and gitignored; measuring them would make the gate answer differently depending on whether someone had run a build, which is not a gate. Their bytes are already inside the committed worklet bundle that is budgeted.

census.note: Any tracked file under these roots at or above the threshold must be budgeted or excluded below. Without this rule the list is one somebody has to remember to extend, and the next large artifact simply is not covered.

artifacts.note: Electron host worklet. The largest file in the repository and, until this gate, measured by nothing.
Expo host worklet, shipped into the mobile app. Carries the compiled wasm contracts inline, which is why it tracks the desktop bundle's size.
Generated Guida compiler asset; regenerated by `npm run generate:guida-compiler-asset`.
The Handbook ships as a mini-app package, so this is a bundle peers actually transfer.
Vendored and pinned, so the ceiling is deliberately tight: this file has no reason to grow, and a change to it should be a decision rather than a diff nobody sized.
Contract wasm executes inside a peer's runtime; size is a cost every node carries.
Below the census threshold, but budgeted anyway: its two sibling contracts are, and covering two of three would be an accident waiting to be relied on.

excluded.reason: CocoaPods checkout of third-party sources, not TwistedPear's shipped bytes.
Untracked build output; its bytes are already counted inside the committed worklet bundle.
